The 2000 United States House of Representatives election for the 1st district in Illinois took place on November 7, 2000, to elect a representative from ___E:Illinois's 1st congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_1st_congressional_district)___ for the ___E:107th United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/107th_United_States_Congress)___ . ___E:Incumbent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incumbent)___ ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ Representative ___E:Bobby Rush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Rush)___ faced a primary challenge from ___E:Illinois Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Senate)___ and future ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .
Rush defeated Obama 61 percent to 30 percent, with other candidates combining for the remaining nine percent.

Rush later defeated his ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ opponent, ___E:Raymond Wardingley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Wardingley)___ , 88 percent to 12 percent, ensuring his reelection.

Subsequent to this election, Obama was ___E:elected to the Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_Senate_election_in_Illinois)___ in 2004, and later ___E:elected President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election)___ in 2008.

___E:Illinois's 1st congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois%27s_1st_congressional_district)___ is a ___E:minority-majority district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minority-majority_state)___ .
At the time of the election, 65 percent of its constituents were ___E:African American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American)___ .

In ___E:redistricting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redistricting)___ after the ___E:1990 United States census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_United_States_census)___ , the district was extended into the suburbs for the first time in 90 years, but a majority of the districts' residents (70%) lived in Chicago.

A strongly ___E:Democratic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ district, only twice since 1966 has a ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ candidate for ___E:United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ received over 20% of the vote.
Rush was involved in the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ of the 1960s.

He was a member of the ___E:Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_Nonviolent_Coordinating_Committee)___ (SNCC) and a former member and founder of the Illinois chapter of the ___E:Black Panther Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Panther_Party)___ .

After coordinating a medical clinic that treated ___E:sickle cell anemia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sickle_cell_anemia)___ , Rush served as an ___E:alderman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderman)___ and was first elected to represent Illinois's 1st district in ___E:1992 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)___ .

Rush ran for ___E:Mayor of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Chicago)___ against ___E:Richard M. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_M._Daley)___ in 1999 and lost, receiving only 28% of the vote, making him appear electorally vulnerable.

Obama, at age 38, was a lecturer at the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ and a two-term ___E:state Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Senate)___ .

Though friends, including ___E:Terry Link U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Link)___ , his colleague in the Illinois Senate, warned Obama against challenging Rush, as there was no obvious reason to displace him to the voters,  Obama ran anyway because of his frustration with what he claimed was Republican obstructionism in the Illinois Legislature and the feeling Rush was representing the district less effectively than Obama could.

Also challenging Rush were ___E:Donne Trotter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donne_Trotter)___ , a state senator, and George Roby, a police officer.  ___E:Raymond Wardingley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Wardingley)___ , a ___E:perennial candidate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perennial_candidate)___ who worked as a ___E:clown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clown)___ , ran unopposed for the Republican nomination.

Obama entered the race in late September 1999, six months before the primary, stating that Rush represented "a politics that is rooted in the past, a reactive politics that isn’t good at coming up with concrete solutions." He promised to build consensus and lead coalitions involving people outside of the black community to reduce crime, improve health care coverage, promote economic development and expand educational opportunities.
Early polling showed Rush's name recognition started off at 90 percent, with Obama's at 11 percent.
Rush had 70 percent approval, while Obama had 8 percent approval.
In the head-to-head matchup, forty-seven percent of the people polled favored Rush, 10 percent favored Obama, and 5 percent supported Trotter, who is also African American.
Most of Obama's support came from ___E:White Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans)___ .

In mid-October, Rush's son, Huey, was murdered, leading Obama to put his campaign on hold.  ___E:Governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Illinois)___ ___E:George Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Ryan)___ called the Illinois Legislature to a special session to re-enact a package of ___E:gun control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control)___ bills, a pet issue of Rush, which had been overturned by the ___E:Illinois Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Supreme_Court)___ .
Obama supported the package, but the session dragged on towards Christmas.

Obama annually spent the Christmas vacation in ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ with his family visiting his grandmother, who raised him. Obama left Illinois, expecting the session would continue into January.
However, a crucial vote took place earlier than expected, failing by five votes with Obama and others absent.

Obama came under fire for missing the vote though he said he would have flown back sooner, but his 18-month-old daughter was sick.  Meanwhile, Rush received an outpouring of sympathy that aided his campaign.

As Obama lived in ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ , a more affluent neighborhood with a higher percentage of White voters than the rest of the district, the narrative of the race became "the Black Panther against the professor."  Obama frequently came off as uptight.
Rush criticized Obama: "Barack Obama went to Harvard and became an educated fool. We’re not impressed with these folks with these Eastern elite degrees.

Barack is a person who read about the civil-rights protests and thinks he knows all about it."  Trotter said, "Barack is viewed in part to be the white man in blackface in our community."   Though the Chicago Tribune endorsed Obama,  many, including local officials, ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ , and ___E:Vice President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Al Gore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore)___ , the ___E:Democratic Party nominee for President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election)___ , endorsed Rush.  Then-State Representative ___E:Tom Dart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Dart)___ supported Obama and organized on his behalf in the 19th ward.

Obama raised enough money to remain competitive with Rush.   However, he neither connected with the working-class African Americans of the district nor provided a convincing reason for them to vote against Rush.  Obama later wrote: "Less than halfway into the campaign, I knew in my bones that I was going to lose. Each morning from that point forward I awoke with a vague sense of dread, realizing that I would have to spend the day smiling and shaking hands and pretending that everything was going according to plan."
Obama later said about his loss to Rush "I got my rear end handed to me"  and acknowledged his own hubris.

However, many analysts believe that Obama's loss helped him to learn from his mistakes, which enabled him to run more successful campaigns in ___E:2004 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_election_in_Illinois,_2004)___ and ___E:2008 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election)___ .
Obama was seen as a stiff policy wonk, and he used the experience to hone his ability to connect with voters.

According to ___E:Chicago City Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_City_Council)___ member ___E:Toni Preckwinkle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Preckwinkle)___ , an early Obama supporter, Obama "took a hard look at himself after that campaign and became a much better campaigner, more at ease on the campaign trail."  He put more effort into his campaign, hiring ___E:David Axelrod U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Axelrod_(political_consultant))___ as his chief political strategist.
Also, Obama increased his focus on the Illinois Senate, improving his legislative accomplishments.
In 2004, Obama was the keynote speaker at the ___E:Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Convention)___ .
After his speech, political pundits speculated about his future as a possible presidential candidate.

After being elected to the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ that year, and amid much speculation in the media regarding his future plans, Obama announced that he would seek the 2008 Democratic presidential nomination in February 2007   and went on to defeat fellow senator ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ in one of the closest presidential nomination races in American history.

He then defeated ___E:John McCain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain)___ , also a senator, in the general election to become ___E:President of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ .
He was ___E:re-elected in 2012. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election,_2012)___
Bobby Rush served a total of thirty years in the House of Representatives, retiring in early 2023 after 15 terms.
